claims.evidence: StatPearls: paired triangular-shaped organs on the superior aspect of each kidney, part of the endocrine system.
OpenStax: cortex makes aldosterone and cortisol; medulla epinephrine and norepinephrine drive fight-or-flight. StatPearls: zones make steroids from cholesterol.
SfE: stress drives ACTH and cortisol, adrenaline prepares for fight or flight; Aldosterone page: governs salt and water balance.
StatPearls: glands on superior aspect of each kidney, within renal (Gerota's) fascia; exact page may be the StatPearls Kidneys article.
StatPearls: right suprarenal gland pyramidal, left crescentic; same article's opening calls both triangular. Reworded to source terms.
claims.newSentence: Triangular overall; the right gland is pyramidal and the left crescentic

claims.evidence: OpenStax: outer cortex, inner medulla, three cortical zones, connective tissue capsule surrounding the gland.
OpenStax: outermost zone aldosterone, intermediate zone glucocorticoids/cortisol, deepest zone androgens.
OpenStax: medulla releases the amine hormones epinephrine and norepinephrine.
StatPearls (Adrenal Hemorrhage): superior, middle, inferior adrenal arteries arise from inferior phrenic artery, abdominal aorta, renal artery. Origins named.
claims.newSentence: Superior suprarenal (from the inferior phrenic), middle suprarenal (from the aorta) and inferior suprarenal (from the renal artery) arteries

claims.evidence: StatPearls: venous drainage 'often' a single adrenal vein; variation common, double left veins common. 'One vein per gland' overstated.
claims.newSentence: Often a single vein per gland; the left drains into the left renal vein and the right directly into the inferior vena cava

claims.evidence: StatPearls: triangular organs on superior aspect of each kidney; enclosed within renal (Gerota's) fascia.
StatPearls adrenal article notes the glands are also known as suprarenal glands.
StatPearls: 'The right suprarenal gland is pyramidal, while the left suprarenal gland is crescentic in shape.' Reworded to that.
claims.newSentence: The two glands differ in shape: the right gland is pyramidal, whereas the left is crescentic (crescent-shaped).

claims.evidence: StatPearls places right gland below the liver, posterior to inferior vena cava, anterior to diaphragm. 'Close to' changed to 'below'.
claims.newSentence: The right gland lies below the liver, behind the inferior vena cava and in front of the diaphragm.

claims.evidence: StatPearls (Adrenal Hemorrhage): outer mesodermally derived cortex; inner medulla originates from the neural crest.
OpenStax: 'outer cortex of glandular tissue and an inner medulla of nervous tissue'; figure caption: connective tissue capsule.
StatPearls physiology: three zones making steroids from cholesterol; OpenStax names the zones and hormone classes.
OpenStax: zona glomerulosa makes mineralocorticoids, named for effect on sodium and potassium; 'fluid and electrolyte' wording not retrieved. Reworded.
claims.newSentence: The outermost zona glomerulosa makes mineralocorticoids, mainly aldosterone, which affect body minerals, especially sodium and potassium.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: intermediate zone makes glucocorticoids; cortisol increases blood glucose. StatPearls: cortisol is the predominant glucocorticoid.
claims.newSentence: The middle zona fasciculata makes glucocorticoids, chiefly cortisol, which raise blood glucose levels.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: deepest zone makes androgens. 'Small amounts' and 'supplement gonadal hormones' not retrieved; trimmed to supported core.
claims.newSentence: The innermost zona reticularis makes androgens, a class of steroid sex hormones.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: medulla releases amine hormones; epinephrine produced in greater quantities than norepinephrine.
claims.newSentence: The medulla at the core of the gland makes the amine hormones adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), and adrenaline is made in greater quantities.

claims.evidence: StatPearls (Adrenal Hemorrhage): 'one of the most well-perfused organs in the human body'. Reworded.
claims.newSentence: The adrenal glands are among the most well-perfused organs in the body.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: superior, middle, inferior adrenal arteries from inferior phrenic artery, abdominal aorta and renal artery. Origin of middle artery added.
claims.newSentence: Arterial blood reaches each gland from several sources: the superior suprarenal arteries (branches of the inferior phrenic arteries), the middle suprarenal arteries (from the abdominal aorta) and the inferior suprarenal arteries (from the renal arteries).

claims.evidence: StatPearls: venous drainage 'often' a single adrenal vein; double left veins also common. Absolute 'each gland' contradicted; 'hilum' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: Each gland is often drained by a single adrenal vein, although variations are common, particularly on the left.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: left adrenal vein to left renal vein, right directly to inferior vena cava. The 'because' explanation was not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The left adrenal vein drains into the left renal vein, whereas the right adrenal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava.

claims.evidence: OpenStax Biology for AP Courses: acetylcholine from preganglionic sympathetic fibres stimulates medullary hormone release; 17.6 not explicit. Citation changed.
OpenStax: medulla handles acute short-term stress via sympathetic system, fight-or-flight; SfE: adrenaline with noradrenaline prepares for fight or flight.
OpenStax: hypothalamic CRH triggers pituitary ACTH, which stimulates cortex corticosteroids; SfE: ACTH promotes cortisol production by the cortex.
Immune and metabolism wording not retrieved from SfE. SfE links stress to ACTH and cortisol; OpenStax: cortisol raises glucose. Standard physiology.
StatPearls (Endocrine Hormones): cortisol negative feedback loop on hypothalamus, anterior pituitary, adrenal gland inhibits CRH, ACTH, cortisol. SfE text not returned.
claims.newSentence: Cortisol has a negative feedback loop that acts on the hypothalamus, anterior pituitary and adrenal gland to inhibit the release of corticotrophin-releasing hormone (CRH), ACTH and cortisol.

claims.evidence: SfE Aldosterone page: steroid governing salt and water balance, which affects blood pressure.
StatPearls physiology: angiotensin II acts on outer cortex, switches on aldosterone synthase, driving aldosterone production in zona glomerulosa.
SfE adrenal page: Cushing's syndrome (overactive) and Addison's disease (underactive); glands described as rarely over- or underactive.
SfE: Addison's is primary adrenal insufficiency; cortex fails to supply cortisol, aldosterone and sex steroids. 'Androgens' reworded to 'sex steroids'.
claims.newSentence: In Addison's disease, also called primary adrenal insufficiency, the glands are underactive and the cortex fails to supply cortisol, aldosterone and sex steroids.

claims.evidence: NIDDK: autoimmune disease causes most cases in developed countries. NHS: immune response targets outer adrenal layer, disrupting cortisol and aldosterone.
claims.newSentence: In developed countries, autoimmune disease is the usual cause: the immune system targets the outer layer of the adrenal gland, which disrupts production of cortisol and aldosterone.

claims.evidence: NHS: early symptoms resemble depression or flu. NIDDK: fatigue, muscle weakness, appetite and weight loss; skin darkening 'may' occur. 'Distinguishing' dropped.
claims.newSentence: Early symptoms can resemble depression or flu. Common symptoms include fatigue, muscle weakness, loss of appetite and weight loss, and people with Addison's disease may also have darkening of the skin.

claims.evidence: NIDDK: adrenal crisis is the most serious complication; NHS: medical emergency. Triggers (infection, injury, surgery) and 'worse very quickly' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: An adrenal crisis is the most serious complication of adrenal insufficiency and is a medical emergency.

claims.evidence: NIDDK: arises when the body makes too much cortisol. NHS: caused by too much cortisol. SfE: excessive cortisol production.
NHS: long-term high-dose steroids most common cause; NIDDK: tumours, usually noncancerous, of pituitary or adrenal glands. 'Cushing's disease' label is textbook.
claims.newSentence: Long-term use of high-dose steroid medicine is the most common cause, and tumours of the pituitary or adrenal glands, usually non-cancerous, can also cause it; when the pituitary is responsible it is called Cushing's disease.

claims.evidence: NHS: more fat on neck, upper back, chest, tummy; red round face; easy bruising, stretch marks; muscle weakness. 'Weight gain' reworded.
claims.newSentence: Features include more body fat on the neck, upper back, chest and tummy, a red, round face, easy bruising, stretch marks and muscle weakness.

claims.evidence: MedlinePlus: adrenals make too much aldosterone; very high blood pressure. Adenoma is a common cause (Genetics); 'most often' and 'Conn syndrome' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: In primary hyperaldosteronism, the adrenal glands make too much aldosterone, and blood pressure can become very high. A non-cancerous tumour in one adrenal gland, called an aldosterone-producing adenoma, is a common cause.

claims.evidence: NCI: 'Surgery to remove the adrenal gland (adrenalectomy) is often used to treat adrenocortical carcinoma.'
NCI page gave no such text in 3 searches. MedlinePlus: rare adrenal tissue tumour, excess epinephrine/norepinephrine, attacks of symptoms. 'Paroxysmal' label not found.
claims.newSentence: Phaeochromocytoma is a rare tumour of adrenal gland tissue that releases too much adrenaline and noradrenaline, and most people with it have attacks of symptoms such as headaches, palpitations, sweating and high blood pressure.

claims.evidence: NIDDK: symptoms come on slowly, may be overlooked or confused with other illnesses. 'Need assessment by a clinician' not retrieved and advice-like.
claims.newSentence: Because the symptoms of Addison's disease come on slowly, they may be overlooked or confused with other illnesses.

claims.evidence: NHS: blood tests measure levels of sodium, potassium and cortisol when Addison's is suspected.
claims.newSentence: In suspected Addison's disease, blood tests measure the levels of sodium, potassium and cortisol.

claims.evidence: NIDDK: ACTH stimulation test used most often; blood test can detect antibodies in autoimmune Addison's disease.
NHS: cortisol measured in blood, urine or saliva; high level may lead to endocrinologist referral and further tests. 'Leads' hedged to 'may lead'.
claims.newSentence: For suspected Cushing's syndrome, cortisol can be checked in blood, urine or saliva, and a high result may lead to referral to an endocrinologist (a hormone specialist), who may arrange further tests on the pituitary and adrenal glands, such as blood tests and scans.

claims.evidence: NIDDK: Cushing's syndrome diagnosis based on medical history, physical exam and lab tests. Scoped to Cushing's syndrome.
claims.newSentence: For Cushing's syndrome, diagnosis is based on the medical history, a physical examination and laboratory tests.

notes: 1) Pyramidal/crescentic confirmed twice from StatPearls NBK482264, but that article's opening also calls both glands triangular; key fact keeps 'triangular overall'. 2) 'Below the liver' is the source's wording; 'close to' removed. 3) NCI phaeochromocytoma page returned no definition or symptom text in 3 searches; sentence rebuilt from MedlinePlus (ency 000340), NCI pheo reference dropped, 'paroxysmal attacks' label not found and removed. 4) Gerota's fascia confirmed at publisher level only (a StatPearls article); the exact page may be the Kidneys article NBK482385 rather than NBK482264. 5) Adrenal crisis triggers (infection, injury, surgery) were not in any NHS or NIDDK text returned; removed, restore only after reading the full NIDDK page. 6) 'Single adrenal vein' stated as absolute was overstated: StatPearls says 'often' single and double left veins are common; hilum not retrieved. 7) Hyperaldosteronism: 'most often' tumour and 'Conn syndrome' not confirmed; kept adenoma as 'a common cause'. 8) Society for Endocrinology text on cortisol effects and feedback was not returned from the cited page; feedback now cited to StatPearls Endocrine Hormones (NBK538498), and c29 kept as textbook. 9) Textbook uses: c29 (cortisol effects) and the Cushing's disease label in c39 (2 of about 5 allowed). 10) References added: NBK555911, NBK538498, SfE Aldosterone, OpenStax Biology for AP Courses, MedlinePlus Genetics, MedlinePlus Pheochromocytoma; all 19 are cited. Page-level attributions for NBK555911 and NBK538498 rest on the search summaries. 11) Words rose from 830 to 885 (intro plus sections) because a few unsupported clauses were replaced by retrieved detail (right adrenal vein, NHS mechanism, MedlinePlus symptom list); trim if a minimal diff is preferred. 12) The search tool returns summaries, not page text, so quotes are as reported by the tool.
